gates.description: Run the four ClaimGuard local gates in order and report each result
gates.template: Run the ClaimGuard local gates in this exact order, stopping at the first failure: 1) `uv run ruff check .`  2) `uv run ruff format --check .`  3) `uv run pyright`  4) `uv run pytest -m "not llm and not e2e" -q`. Report the outcome of each gate as PASS or FAIL with the first actionable error. If `uv` is not on PATH, say so and stop - do not substitute pip or python -m.

spec-audit.description: Map ClaimGuard spec sections to implementing files and report drift, gaps, contradictions
spec-audit.template: Audit ClaimGuard for docs-vs-code drift. Map every spec section in docs/05 sections 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7; docs/04 sections 4, 6, 9; docs/06 section 5; and docs/09 Part B to the file under claimguard/ that implements it, and mark each EXISTING, PARTIAL, or MISSING. Then list contradictions, specifically: the Severity and Tone enums in claimguard/contracts.py versus the SQL CHECK constraints in claimguard/db/migrations/versions/0001_initial_schema.sql; and any doc that still references the retired docs/07 or docs/08. Output one markdown table plus a 'top 5 risks' list. Do not edit any file.

engine-smoke.description: Smoke-check the flagship fixture CLM-0042 end to end
engine-smoke.template: Smoke-check the ClaimGuard flagship claim CLM-0042. Expected outcome: the bundle parses into a CanonicalClaim whose dense payload exposes exactly three published defects - COV-001 (coverage periodEnd earlier than anchorDate), AUTH-004 (no authorization present), DUP-002 (two identical lines). First check whether claimguard/pipeline.py and claimguard/cli/main.py exist. If they do, run the validation and show the findings as JSON. If they do not exist yet, run `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_payload_contract.py tests/unit/test_fhir_parse.py -q` and report which of the three defects are already provable in code and which engine pieces are still missing. Do not implement anything.
